subject: Biology
summary: Covers human pathology and immunology: Spectrum of human pathogens (Bacterial: Typhoid, Pneumonia; Viral: Common cold, Dengue, Chikungunya; Helminthic: Filariasis, Ascariasis; Protozoan: Amoebiasis; Fungal: Ringworm), Dual-host life cycle of Plasmodium and malarial pathogenesis (Hemozoin toxin), Innate immunity barriers (Physical, Physiological, Cellular, Cytokine Interferons), Acquired immunity (Humoral H2L2 antibodies, Cell-Mediated CMI and graft rejection), Five immunoglobulin isotypes (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD), Active vs Passive immunity and vaccine biotechnology (Hepatitis B recombinant in yeast), Allergic hypersensitivity cascade and Autoimmunity, Cancer biology (loss of contact inhibition, metastasis, carcinogens, alpha-interferon immunotherapy), HIV/AIDS virology (Reverse transcriptase, Macrophage HIV factory, CD4+ T-cell collapse), Pharmacology of abused substances (Opioids/Heroin, Cannabinoids, Cocaine dopamine reuptake, Hallucinogens), and Alcohol/Tobacco pathology.

sections.title: Pathogens & Parasitic Human Diseases: Spectrum & Vectors
sections.topic: Bacterial, Viral, Helminthic, Protozoan, & Fungal Pathologies

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pathogens encompass Bacteria (Typhoid - Widal test; Pneumonia - fluid alveoli), Viruses (Common cold - Rhinovirus; Dengue - Aedes), Helminths (Filariasis - Culex, Ascariasis), Protozoans (Amoebiasis - Entamoeba), and Fungi (Ringworm).

sections.codeSnippet:
HUMAN PATHOGEN CLASSES
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┼──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼              ▼              ▼                  ▼
  BACTERIAL          VIRAL           PROTOZOAN      HELMINTHIC          FUNGAL
  ├── Typhoid        ├── Common Cold ├── Malaria    ├── Filariasis      └── Ringworm
  └── Pneumonia      ├── Dengue      └── Amoebiasis └── Ascariasis
                     └── Chikungunya
sections.content:
### 1.1 Pathogen Classification & Clinical Spectrum
- **Bacterial**: Typhoid (*S. typhi*, Widal test) and Pneumonia (*S. pneumoniae*, alveoli fluid).
- **Viral**: Common cold (*Rhinovirus*, nose/upper passage), Dengue & Chikungunya (*Aedes aegypti*).
- **Helminthic & Others**: Filariasis (*Wuchereria*, *Culex* vector), Amoebiasis (*Entamoeba*), Ringworm (*Microsporum*).

sections.title: Life Cycle of Plasmodium & Malarial Pathogenesis
sections.topic: Dual-Host Schizogony, Hemozoin Toxin, & Anopheles Vector Transmission

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Plasmodium dual-host cycle: Human (asexual liver and RBC schizogony releasing Hemozoin fever toxin) and Mosquito (sexual gut syngamy, ookinete, oocyst, and sporozoite salivary migration).

sections.codeSnippet:
PLASMODIUM DUAL-HOST LIFE CYCLE
                        
    HUMAN HOST (Asexual Cycle / Intermediate)      MOSQUITO HOST (Sexual Cycle / Definitive)
    
  Anopheles bite injects SPOROZOITES            Female Anopheles ingests GAMETOCYTES
                 │                                                │
  Liver Schizogony (Exo-erythrocytic)               Syngamy in Mosquito Midgut Stomach
                 │                                                │
  Erythrocytic Schizogony (RBCs)                    Ookinete ──► Oocyst ──► Sporogony
                 │                                                │
  RBC Rupture releases HEMOZOIN TOXIN            SPOROZOITES migrate to Salivary Glands
  (Causes cyclic high fever & chills)                             │
                 │                                                ▼
  Forms Gametocytes (n) ─────────────────────────► Injected into Human Blood
sections.content:
### 2.1 Malarial Life Cycle
- **Human Stage**: Sporozoites enter liver cells $\rightarrow$ merozoites burst liver cells $\rightarrow$ invade RBCs $\rightarrow$ RBC lysis releases **Hemozoin** (cyclic fever/chills) + gametocytes.
- **Mosquito Stage**: Midgut syngamy $\rightarrow$ motile ookinete $\rightarrow$ oocyst $\rightarrow$ sporozoites in salivary glands.

sections.title: Innate Immunity Barriers & Cytokine Signaling

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Innate immunity: Physical (skin/mucus), Physiological (HCl/lysozyme), Cellular (PMN-neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells), and Cytokines (antiviral Interferons protecting uninfected cells).

sections.codeSnippet:
INNATE IMMUNITY BARRIERS
                                       │
     ┌──────────────────┬──────────────┴──────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                             ▼                  ▼
PHYSICAL BARRIERS   PHYSIOLOGICAL BARRIERS        CELLULAR BARRIERS    CYTOKINE BARRIERS
├── Skin (Keratin)  ├── Stomach HCl (pH 1.8)      ├── PMN-Neutrophils  └── Interferons
└── Mucous Epithelium└── Tears/Saliva (Lysozyme)  ├── Monocytes & Macrophages (IFN-α, β, γ)
                                                  └── Natural Killer (NK) Cells
sections.content:
### 3.1 Innate Barriers
- **Four Barriers**: Physical (Skin, Mucus), Physiological (Stomach $\text{HCl}$, Lysozyme), Cellular (PMNs, Macrophages, NK cells), and Cytokine (Interferons $\text{IFN}-\alpha, \beta, \gamma$).

sections.title: Acquired Immunity: Humoral vs Cell-Mediated & Antibodies
sections.topic: B vs T Lymphocytes, H2L2 Antibody Structure, & Immunoglobulin Isotypes (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Humoral immunity (B-cells, plasma cells, antibodies) vs Cell-Mediated CMI (T-cells, graft rejection). H2L2 antibody structure with disulfide bonds. Isotypes: IgG (placenta), IgA (colostrum), IgM (pentamer), IgE (allergy).

sections.codeSnippet:
ACQUIRED IMMUNITY BRANCHES
                                        │
         ┌──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                             ▼
  HUMORAL IMMUNITY (AMI)                                       CELL-MEDIATED IMMUNITY (CMI)
  ├── Driven by B-Lymphocytes                                 ├── Driven by T-Lymphocytes
  ├── Secretes soluble Antibodies into plasma                  ├── CD4⁺ Helper T-cells & CD8⁺ Cytotoxic T-cells
  └── Fights extracellular bacteria & toxins                   └── Fights intracellular viruses, cancer, & drives
                                                                   GRAFT / ORGAN REJECTION
sections.content:
### 4.1 Acquired Immunity & Antibodies
- **Humoral vs CMI**: B-cells produce plasma antibodies; T-cells drive CMI and graft rejection.
- **Antibody $\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$**: $2\text{ Heavy} + 2\text{ Light chains}$ linked by disulfide bonds. $\text{IgG}$ crosses placenta; $\text{IgA}$ in colostrum.

sections.title: Active vs Passive Immunity & Vaccine Biotechnology
sections.topic: Natural vs Artificial Immunity, Colostrum, ATS, & 1st/2nd/3rd Gen Vaccines

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Active immunity (host builds own antibodies and memory via infection or vaccine) vs Passive immunity (pre-formed antibodies via maternal IgG/IgA or ATS). Recombinant Hepatitis B vaccine produced in yeast.

sections.codeSnippet:
IMMUNITY TYPES
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  ACTIVE IMMUNITY                                         PASSIVE IMMUNITY
  Host produces its OWN antibodies upon antigen contact.   Pre-formed antibodies transferred directly to host.
  ├── Natural: Recovery from chickenpox infection         ├── Natural: Maternal IgG via placenta / IgA in colostrum
  └── Artificial: Vaccination (BCG, Polio, MMR)           └── Artificial: Anti-Tetanus Serum (ATS) / Anti-snake venom
sections.content:
### 5.1 Active vs Passive Immunity
- **Active**: Long-lasting memory (natural recovery, vaccines).
- **Passive**: Immediate, temporary protection (maternal $\text{IgG}/\text{IgA}$, ATS).
- **Vaccines**: $1^{\text{st}}$ gen (whole), $2^{\text{nd}}$ gen (recombinant yeast Hep B), $3^{\text{rd}}$ gen (nucleic acid).

sections.title: Hypersensitivity (Allergies) & Autoimmune Pathologies
sections.topic: Type I IgE Allergy Cascade, Histamine/Serotonin, Anaphylaxis, & Autoimmune Breakdown

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Allergies: Allergen cross-links IgE on mast cells, releasing histamine and serotonin (treated with antihistamines, epinephrine, steroids). Autoimmunity: breakdown of self-tolerance (Rheumatoid arthritis, Myasthenia gravis).

sections.codeSnippet:
ALLERGIC HYPERSENSITIVITY CASCADE
                         
   First Exposure to Allergen ──► B-cells produce excess IgE Antibodies
                                             │
   IgE binds Fc receptors on Mast Cells and Basophils
                                             │
   Re-exposure to Allergen ──► Allergen cross-links IgE ──► Mast Cell Degranulation
                                             │
   Releases Vasoactive Amines: Histamine and Serotonin
                                             │
   Symptoms: Vasodilation, broncho-spasm, watery eyes, running nose, Anaphylaxis
sections.content:
### 6.1 Allergies & Autoimmunity
- **Allergy**: $\text{IgE}$ cross-linking on mast cells releases histamine and serotonin.
- **Autoimmune Disorders**: Rheumatoid arthritis (synovial IgM), Myasthenia gravis (ACh receptor auto-antibodies), Type 1 diabetes, Hashimoto's disease.

sections.title: Cancer Biology: Contact Inhibition & Metastasis
sections.topic: Neoplasia, Oncogenes vs Tumor Suppressors, Carcinogens, & Therapies

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Cancer hallmarks: Loss of contact inhibition (uncontrolled tumors) and Metastasis (invasion of distant organs). Carcinogens: UV, tobacco benzopyrene, oncogenic viruses. Treatment: surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy (Vincristine), and alpha-interferon.

sections.codeSnippet:
CANCER HALLMARKS
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                   ▼
  LOSS OF CONTACT INHIBITION                           METASTASIS
  Normal cells stop dividing when touching adjacent   Cancer cells detach from primary tumor, enter blood/
  cells. Cancer cells lose this property, forming      lymph, and colonize distant organs to form secondary
  unorganized cell masses (Tumors).                   tumors. (Most feared property of cancer).
sections.content:
### 7.1 Cancer Biology
- **Hallmarks**: Loss of contact inhibition, angiogenesis, and **Metastasis** (hallmark of malignancy).
- **Therapies**: Chemotherapy (*Catharanthus* vinca alkaloids: Vincristine/Vinblastine) and Immunotherapy ($\alpha$-Interferon).

sections.title: HIV/AIDS Virology & CD4+ T-Cell Collapse
sections.topic: Retrovirus Structure, Reverse Transcriptase, Macrophage Factory, & Opportunistic Infections

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: HIV (diploid ssRNA retrovirus with reverse transcriptase): gp120 binds CD4 receptors. Macrophages act as persistent HIV factory; CD4+ T-cells burst, collapsing count (<200/μL) leading to fatal opportunistic infections. ELISA screening, Western Blot confirmatory.

sections.codeSnippet:
HIV VIRION STRUCTURE & REPLICATION
                            
   Virion: Diploid ssRNA (2 x ssRNA) + Reverse Transcriptase, Integrase, Protease
           Envelope studded with gp120 and gp41 glycoproteins.
                            │
   Replication:
   gp120 binds CD4⁺ Receptor ──► Viral ssRNA converted to dsDNA via Reverse Transcriptase
   ──► Integrated into host genome via Integrase ──► Viral transcription & budding
   ├── Macrophages: Act as "HIV Factory" (produce virus continuously without dying)
   └── CD4⁺ T-Cells: Burst & deplete (<200/μL) ──► Severe Opportunistic Infections
sections.content:
### 8.1 HIV & AIDS
- **Retrovirus**: $2 \times \text{ssRNA}$, Reverse Transcriptase, $gp120$ spike.
- **Pathogenesis**: Macrophage HIV factory; $\text{CD4}^+$ T-cell destruction ($<200/\mu\text{L}$) causes AIDS.
- **Diagnostics**: ELISA screening, Western Blot confirmation; AZT therapy.

sections.title: Pharmacology of Abused Substances: Opioids, Cannabinoids, & Cocaine
sections.topic: Opioids (Heroin/Morphine), Cannabinoids, Cocaine Dopamine Transport, & Hallucinogens

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Opioids (*Papaver somniferum* - Heroin/diacetylmorphine, CNS/GI depressant); Cannabinoids (*Cannabis sativa* - brain receptors, cardiovascular effects); Cocaine (*Erythroxylum coca* - dopamine reuptake block, CNS stimulant, hallucinations); Hallucinogens (LSD, Datura, Belladonna).

 └── Heroin ("Smack")           └── Marijuana, Hashish, Ganja   └── Cocaine / Crack ("Coke")
sections.content:
### 9.1 Abused Substances
- **Opioids**: Morphine & Heroin (diacetylmorphine, "Smack") from *Papaver somniferum*; CNS/GI depressant.
- **Cannabinoids**: *Cannabis sativa*; affects cardiovascular system.
- **Cocaine**: *Erythroxylum coca*; blocks dopamine reuptake; CNS stimulant.

sections.title: Alcohol & Tobacco Abuse Pathology
sections.topic: Nicotine Adrenal Stimulation, CO Hypoxia, Alcohol Metabolism, Cirrhosis, & Withdrawal Syndrome

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Tobacco: Nicotine stimulates adrenal adrenaline release (raises BP/HR); CO causes hypoxia; carcinogens cause lung/bladder cancer. Alcohol: oxidized to acetaldehyde, causing fatty liver and cirrhosis. Abrupt withdrawal causes tremors, tachycardia, seizures.

sections.codeSnippet:
ADDICTION PATHOPHYSIOLOGY & WITHDRAWAL
                         
   Tobacco (Nicotine) ──► Adrenal Medulla ──► Adrenaline/Noradrenaline (↑ BP & HR)
   Tobacco Smoke      ──► Carbon Monoxide (CO) ──► Carboxyhemoglobin ──► Tissue Hypoxia
   Alcohol (Ethanol)  ──► Acetaldehyde ──► Fatty Liver ──► Cirrhosis of Liver
   Abrupt Cessation   ──► Physical Withdrawal Syndrome (Tremors, Anxiety, Sweating, Seizures)
sections.content:
### 10.1 Tobacco & Alcohol Pathology
- **Tobacco**: Nicotine stimulates adrenal adrenaline (↑ BP & HR); $\text{CO}$ forms carboxyhemoglobin; $3,4$-benzopyrene causes cancer.
- **Alcohol**: Acetaldehyde intermediate causes fatty liver and irreversible **Cirrhosis**; abrupt cessation causes Withdrawal Syndrome.

sections.title: Human Health & Immunology Glossary & High-Yield Traps

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Master human health, pathology, and immunology glossary with 50+ definitions and 10 high-yield NEST misconceptions and diagnostic traps.

sections.content:
### 11.1 Master Human Health Glossary & Traps
- **Common Cold vs Pneumonia**: Rhinovirus infects nose/upper respiratory tract, NOT lungs; Pneumonia infects alveoli.
- **Graft Rejection**: Mediated by CMI (T-cells, $\text{CD8}^+$), NOT B-cells.
- **Placental Antibody**: $\text{IgG}$ is the ONLY antibody that crosses the placenta.
- **Interferons**: Secreted by virus-infected cells to protect healthy neighbors.
